column1: # The latest independent audit of each table: an auditor who did not write the entries drew a random sample of rows graded understood
# and re-derived each from the binaries or the cited specification. real = the entry held up, shallow = true but derived from a name or
# credited without behaviour of its own, wrong = contradicted. sample is small: read it with the percentage. The last row of a table with
# the latest date is the one summary.tsv and docs/coverage.md show.

column7: note

PIC page: 12 claims re-derived from pic.o, pcibr.o and the IP35 PROM; wrong: an unknown part and revision is not rejected (only the debug name changes), and the PROM interrupt-register clear writes 64-bit zero and all-ones to +0x108 and +0x110 on the PIC path (the 32-bit stores at +0x10c, +0x114 and +0x12c are the non-PIC path); shallow: the PIO flush workaround omitted the counter address, the value 1, and the device and pin-mask conditions; also fixed an inverted order of the revision-1 enable clear and the unlisted control-register mask. Census mechanics: 4 of 4 PIC sites right

Bedrock page: 8 claims re-derived from kernel.o and its neighbours; wrong: hub_error_clear (all-ones writes counted as zeroes, 15 slots not 14, two aliases), the +0x1604200 counter reading (bits 13:4 times five at all 52 sites), and the +0x1000090 store attribution (sites belong to symbol-less neighbours); shallow: per_hub_init omitted the slice stores in the second window. Also outside the sample: hub_widget_reset had a loop over eight registers and no polling (wrong), kernel.o has 61 not 71 window literals (wrong). Census mechanics: 4 of 6 Bedrock sites exact, 2 with a dropped run-time displacement or loop-iteration artifact; gp auto-min holds in 11 of 11 objects

Xbow page: 12 claims re-derived from the IP27 xbow.o routines xbow_enable_perf_counter, xbow_reset_link, xbow_prio_bw_alloc and xbow_errintr_handler; all held. Outside the sample: the bandwidth refusal test named the wrong register (the compared byte count is the request rounded to register units and converted back, not the raw request in a3) and was corrected. 8 further claims drawn from the PIC and Bedrock pages (pic_attach2, md_int_block, hubni_print_state) held too

IOC3 page: 4 claims re-derived from ioc3ei.o, ioc3.o and if_ef.o (eiattach writes to 0x38, 0x34 and 0x2c; ioc3_init registration; the MII routines; ioc3_error_handler); shallow: ioc3_error_handler was described as writing 0x40 back, it stores the constant 1 after a valid-bit test and a 13-way jump on bits 4:1. scripts/facts.py failed on that routine (a symbolic table base was formatted as a number); fixed and tested

IOC4 page: 4 claims re-derived from ioc4_pckm.o, sio_ioc4.o and ide.o (the keyboard control store, hardware_init ring bases, ioc4_dma_error_intr, xide_intr_clear with the ATA accessor stride); wrong: the error-address low word's unit is bits 4:2 doubled and added to the character 1, and bit 1 picks the printed word RX or TX, not bits 3:1 as a unit

Bridge and XBridge page: 8 claims re-derived from pcibr.o, xbridge.o and the IP27 kernel; wrong: xbridge_attach does not clear bit 24 of the interrupt enable (the literal 0x00003eff7ffffe00 is ORed in whole; the 0xc0023 test sets record fields), and part 0xd100 tested by xbow_widget_present is read from the crossbar's own identification word, not a Bridge-family chip; shallow: the upper bus error address accessor applies no 15:0 mask

MACE page: 2 claims re-derived from the IP32 kernel.o routines powerintr (byte loads at 0xbf3a0c07, 0xbf3a4a07 and 0xbf3a0a07) and read_dallas_nvram (byte reads from 0xbf3a0e08 plus offset plus index); both held

CRIME page: 3 claims re-derived from the IP32 kernel.o routines intr (returns 0 or 1), mlreset (get_crimerev and flushbus are calls; stores to 0x48, 0x250, 0x8, 0x18, 0x10, 0x30 as written) and the add_ioboard body at 0x8168 (the symbol at 0x8160 is a bare return); all held

Hub page: 9 routine entries of the IP27 kernel and hubspc.o re-derived from the disassembly (ackkgclock/acktmoclock register choice and GOT slots, sn0_skip_dump, hubni_eint_handler string, hub_dmamap_addr flag logic and string, early_pckminit, get_hub_chiprev, hubspc_map, prominfo_add); all held. Outside the sample a duplicate entry of clear_hub_pi_error said word where the code loads and stores doublewords (fixed). Six routines have two entries each in the same kernel (ackkgclock, acktmoclock, bte_avail, bte_disable, callout_time_to_hz, clear_hub_pi_error); the first five pairs agree and the sixth differed only in that width
IOC3 page: ioc3_subdev_enabled and ioc3_poll re-derived from ioc3.o with relocations; both held

HEART page: heart_intr_bits_take re-derived from heart.o; held (lld and scd are doubleword accesses, the entry calls the target a word; the neighbouring entry says 64-bit word). The five later heart commits are not in this clone and were not audited

HEART page, the interrupt, reset and probe re-read (20 of the commit's 33 changed claims drawn with seed 20261102, plus two neighbouring claims read in the same paragraphs), re-derived from IP30 unix with scripts/facts.py: heart_startup (WID_REQ_TIMEOUT 40000 or 128 by kdebug before any registration, widget 0 from 0x9000000010000004, loop 15 to 0 gated by xswitch_info_link_ok), heart_intr (semaphore path for flag 0x1000 with the 28673 split, handler call at 0x...3ff98, CLR_ISR order, +208 count with the -1 adjustment), heart_mlreset store order and CAUSE write-back, heart_mp_intr_init, heart_imr_bits_rmw lock and flushbus delay slot, do_heart_intr_alloc vector formula and free-vector AND-NOT, badaddr and wbadaddr clear sequence (+0x40 doubleword zero, +0x44 word in the reset), the six SYNC reads in dobuserr_common, SET_ISR stores in sendintr, debug_stop_all_cpus and heart_set_cpu_intr. shallow: CLR_ISR was said to be written before the handler for 'vectors 3 and above' although vectors 59 and up go to buserror_intr without a write; heart_set_cpu_intr was said to reach vectors 0 to 31 but sllv sign-extends, so vector 31 sets bits 31 to 63. wrong: the dispatcher count at +208 was said to be the number of vectors served, but the routine adds served minus one (one vector adds 0). All three fixed.
MACE page: pcimh_device_unregister re-derived from pcimh.o; held
CRIME page: the Crime Timer address, table and width re-derived from the specification text; held
GBE page: FRM_2, CRS_0 and VC_2 offsets, field positions and reset states checked against the specification text; held

File-system scope entries: namevno.o, ckpt_procfs.o and dksc.o counts and sizes match functions.tsv and the imports support the roles; shallow: nm_link was called a bare return but sets the constant 18 in the delay slot (fixed). Scope list: sn0drv.o was excluded as having no chip register access although its routines front the router register and Hub vector reads (moved to the keep list), and the four exclusion reasons now say they are by role, not by a scan

CRIME pixel pipeline registers (3 of the changed rows): ScrMask[4] held (loader ld and sd, table bytes, ClipMode bit 5 and bit 0 re-derived); wrong: the Fog.dfdy entry called the specification description a typing slip, but the specification says df/dy there (fixed); shallow: Texture.dqdy omitted that the specification repeats d(1/w)/dx so the y direction is inferred (fixed, label split). Lane re-check because the lane scored under 85 percent: all 88 changed rows checked mechanically for loader displacements, instruction mnemonics and widths, shadow offsets, table bytes, specification size, access and global flag and cited page, and the memory transfer engine and TLB entries re-read in crime_dma.o, crime_retrace.o and crime_tiles.o; no further fault

Classification entries across the chip-driver, file-system and kernel-object scope pages: dmi_register, dsreq, raw_cb, grio2_stream, grio2_fs, tcp_output, vsocket, efs_dalloc and cachefsidbg held (routine counts, sizes and imports re-read with nm); wrong: the IP30 pciio_ppb entry said the object reaches the bridge only through two calls, but it imports 20 pciio calls and its largest routines were not named (fixed); shallow: the IP35 xtalk entry gave 70 routines for 71, and named the Bridge as a served widget although the object names only the Xbow (fixed, Bridge marked inferred). Mechanical check of every member and routine size on the three pages against functions.tsv found no mismatch

Census pages (L1, router scan tunnel, TIOCP): L1 line-status and FIFO-control/interrupt-identity offsets, the scan-chain record allocation of 144 bytes for 1024 bits, the 4,000,000 receive time-out, and the l3_bigend dead path re-read in the relocatable objects and held; wrong: the TIOCP page said pic.o and the USB driver carry the tiocp.h name in both builds, but only the IP35 set holds them (the IP27 set has usrpci.o there) (fixed)

Route tags and the ordered list (20 of the 7 triage commits' changed items, drawn at random across the tagged entries, ordered steps and corrections): Xbow large-routine addresses (all twelve are PROM routines whose link-block displacements 0x100 to 0x13c were re-read and none is a config seed), IOC3 UART lane (line-control byte at UART+3 re-read in set_baud_ti and hardware_init), IOC4 xide_intr_clear (doubleword index 0 then 4 of the interrupt block), the IOC4/IOC3/Hub/Bedrock stale-census and duplicate tags (configs and census output checked), the Hub register routines, ordered-step function names (present in the held objects), harness limits (pcireg gp loads) and the missing-source tags (all seven public trees are empty submodules) held; wrong: the MACE video bits 35:32 entry said the specification defines only bits 18:0, but its video hardware configuration table names bits 35:32 the MACE revision code, so the entry is answered, not open (entry deleted, MACE page now established); shallow: the Hub unnamed-role routine list omitted hub_piomap_free, an unnamed routine and hub_ioerror_handler (added). Same-pattern faults outside the sample, fixed: the HEART refused-access, CRIME unreached-registers and CRIME transfer-engine tags called the held but stripped diagnostics a missing binary

IP27 and IP30 kernel routine entries of the Hub, Bridge, HEART and timer pages (20 of the 31 commits' promoted rows, seed 20261102): Bridge-family pcireg accessors (pci_bus_addr_addr_get, type1_cntr_get, tflush_get, dirmap_wid_set, intr_dst_set, rrb_bit_set, map_fault_get, control_bit_clr, intr_host_err_get, intr_dst_target_id_get, intr_dst_addr_set), intr_disconnect_level, hub_widgetdev_shutdown, timein_body, nanotime_syscall, wbadaddr_val and heart_intrd_start re-read instruction by instruction with offsets, widths, panic and assfail strings and line numbers held; wrong: log_tstamp_event said the private ring wraps when the pointer is below the limit (it advances below the limit and wraps otherwise) and that issplprof only gates the level raise (a nonzero answer ends the routine before any wake-up, and the tests are repeated after spl1) (fixed); shallow: the IP27 int_ate_addr entry omitted that a negative index fails the bound check, and heart_dmamap_drain credited the IP30 kernel row from an entry that named only the object copy (both fixed)

IP27 io, jlimits and kmem kernel-object entries (20 of the 22 entries of the classification commit, seed 20261102): routine counts, member sizes, named routine sizes and import lists re-read with readelf for all 20, and the routine bodies re-read in the disassembly; counts, sizes and imports all held. wrong (3): idbgentry.o was called a table of command entries that idbg_setup builds, but it is a set of 36-byte stubs calling through the idbgfuncs pointer; job_as_exit was said to add usage at exit, but it unlinks and frees an address-space record; the job-ID table credited its zone to jobtab_zone when jidtab_init creates its own. shallow (4): device_admin_info_set was called a table fill (it sets INTR_TARGET and INTR_SWLEVEL on the descriptor or a label), hwcopy named only a role (it copies in 16-bit units with a byte fallback), dma.o was framed as DMA mapping for a device when the code maps a buffer's pages into kernel virtual space and programs no DMA, and the kmem_debug zone import list omitted nested_64bitunlock. Also reworded as role-only: the debug-monitor loader and lan.o (both stubs print a not-supported message). Sample real-rate 65 percent, so all 22 entries were re-checked: the two undrawn entries (alenlist, kmem_debug mbuf) held and the others now say what the code does. All faults fixed

Answers from the six answer commits (20 of 30 changed items, seed 20261102): Hub spool entry layout, the 0x2000c8/d0/d8/e0 notes, the big-window table at 0x400160 to 0x400190, the II error level 64 allocator chain, MD directory error decode, response buffer fields and the PIC revision 1 constant, direct-map set-up, xide_intr_clear and its index 4 read, ATA DMA start, completion and init, the PIC error dump skip rules and call groups (spot-checked), Bridge revision 2 enable mask re-read from the object; wrong: the hardwired interrupt table lists level 105 but not 106 (same name string), the Bridge interrupt device note limited pcibr_intr_alloc to pins below 4 (the loop runs 0 to 7), and the IOC4 DMA table called the index 7 stores byte writes (the accessor stores the whole word); all three fixed; also fixed outside the sample: the direct-map setters call panic for type -1 and ignore other types rather than printing through cmn_err

Unresolved window-pointer table of the IOC3 page (11 of the 5 census-refresh commits' items drawn at random, seed 20261102, ioc3 share): inventory summary counts, flushbus, spl7, qprintf, hwgraph_path_add, the 98-call count and its 43/12/43 split, the 40 indirect calls and their per-function split, ioc3_read's indirect call, the IP35 kernel absence and the sio_unlock_port rows re-read from the kernels and objects; shallow: hub_check_pci_equiv compared 'NASID bits' only (the body also needs equal window bytes and low 24 address bits; reworded), and the ioc3_read and sio_unlock_port function rows were credited in builds (IP30 ioc3_read, IP32 serialio) whose code the entries did not describe (entries now say so); wrong: nic_ioc3_vertex_info said it stores 0x200000 as a configuration-space offset and never reads its window argument, but its third argument is window+0x34 so it writes the GPIO control-set register (fixed, and the same store in nic_get_eaddr, which also passes window+0x30 on to nic_eaddr, added to both entries and to the 0x34 row); same-pattern, outside the sample: the us_delay entry treated the IP30 body as the IP27 counter wait (rewritten from the IP30 body)

Crossbow census regenerated against the specification map (6 drawn items plus a full re-check of every item of the commit): the 39 added site rows (opcode and displacement matched against the three PROM disassemblies, 39 of 39), the 491-versus-452 site count, the eight Reserved rows (one IP35 PROM routine writing 0xff to each word and reading it back), the XB_ID and XB_CTRL counts and the XB_CTRL 0x80000000 store held; wrong: the generator names every link slot from 0x108 to 0x1d8 XB_LINK_IBUF_FLUSH because it treats the specification's 0x100 + 64xn family as a range (0x108 is link control, 0x130 reset, 0x198 and 0x1d8 arbitration upper of links 10 and 11), and fields.tsv holds a shift-0 field that is a delay-slot no-operation and mask/shift fields taken from the wrong register at one IP27 PROM site; the tables cannot be edited by hand and the shared join tool is outside this repository, so the xbow page now says how to read the rows and the fix is handed over as a patch

HEART census report text (3 items): the no-spec statement and the empty touched-but-absent list held; shallow: the empty touched-but-absent, disagreement and unreached lists say 'None' although no datasheet or specification is compared in no-spec mode (tool text); wrong: the report and its commit message call 84 rows the window-pointer calls 'distinct sites in the kernel's interrupt set-up routine', but the rows are one per argument register: 69 distinct calls spread over 49 routines of the kernel and PROM, only 9 of them in the interrupt set-up routine (the shared report tool counts rows; the same fault was fixed by hand for IOC3 in the earlier triage, and the count is left for the tool fix)

IP27 io, jlimits and kmem kernel-object entries (20 of the 22 entries of the classification commit, seed 20261102): routine counts, member sizes, named routine sizes and import lists re-read with readelf for all 20, and the routine bodies of ddi, devsupport, disksub, dma, sgset, lan, vme, volume_support, dbg, idbgentry, ioerror_handling, hwcopy, jlimits, jid, jl_pproc and the kmem pairs re-read in the disassembly; counts, sizes and imports all held. wrong (3): idbgentry.o was called a table of command entries whose idbg_setup builds it, but the member is a set of 36-byte stubs that call through the idbgfuncs pointer and holds no table (idbg_setup calls slot 1 and then debug); jl_pproc job_as_exit was said to add usage at exit, but it unlinks and frees an address-space record (and proc_job_accum also checks the limit and sends signal 9); the job-ID table entry credited its zone to jobtab_zone when jidtab_init creates its own; shallow (3): devsupport device_admin_info_set was called a table fill (it sets INTR_TARGET and INTR_SWLEVEL on the descriptor or a label), hwcopy named only a role (it copies in 16-bit units with a byte fallback), and the kmem_debug zone import list omitted nested_64bitunlock. Also reworded outside the sample, as role-only: dbg and lan. Sample real-rate 70 percent, so all 22 entries were re-checked: the two unsampled entries (alenlist, kmem_debug kern_mbuf) held, and the other 20 now say what the disassembly shows. All faults fixed

Commit 9f7c1b3 added the IP35 ioc4.o routines. The four understood rows (console read, subdev enables, enable and disable) were re-derived from the IP35 ioc4.o object and checked against the IP27 ioc3.o copies: the words are identical (6, 11, 17 and 18), and only the call relocation name differs (ioc4_subdev_ptr for ioc3_subdev_ptr), as the entries say. Return paths, the sllv bit mask and the LL/SC loops were traced. The pinned root manifest matched before reading. Wrong: none. Shallow: none. One prose slip fixed: the console entry put its lw at 0x101c; it is at 0x1020 (0x101c is the delay-slot li). The ioc4_subdev_ptr row is named-only and was not graded.

Commit 9f7c1b3 gave the IP27 kernel pcibr_open row its own derivation (understood, sample 1 of the commit changes). Re-derived from the IP27/unix body: 52 bytes, 13 words identical to xbow_open, both call cap_able_cred at the same address, the dsll32 in the delay slot builds 1<<37, and the return value is 1 when cap_able_cred returns zero. The four located pcibr_open copies (IP27 pcibr.o, IP30 unix, IP30 pcibr.o, IP35 pcibr.o) were also checked and share the same words (only the jal target differs). Wrong: none. Shallow: none. The sample is one row, so read it as a spot check.

Wave 1 hardware-facing explanations of 42 CRIME and IP32 kernel routines, audited before landing against hostfacts and the disassembly. A 12-draft sample stratified by object (crime.o 1, crime_init.o 2, crime_retrace.o 1, kernel.o 8) came out 8 wrong, 2 shallow and 2 real, so all 42 were audited; counts are of the drafts before repair and all 31 wrong or shallow ones were then repaired. Wrong, by kind: 17 gave a masked or modified value as a constant or as written back unchanged (the bit clears of CRIME Software Interrupt bits 28 and 29 and of the RTC-block bytes, the ISA DMA buffer address mask, the delay calibration scale and divide, the interrupt mask merges), 5 inverted or dropped control flow (crimeInitInfo, gbeRun, VEC_int, get_crimerev, gbeStartVideoTiming), 1 misplaced a table address (crime_init), 1 read a called pointer as an argument (crimeRetraceHandler). Shallow: Unknowns the disassembly answers and coprocessor-0 work the bundle hides (spl0, _cpuclkper100ticks), plus two routines with large unexplained halves (crime_setvideotiming, crimevec_intrd).
